// ======================================
// Build Ollama Chat Payload
// ======================================

return items.map(item => {

  const job = item.json;

  // -----------------------------
  // Extract fields safely
  // -----------------------------

  const jobTitle = job.job_title || "";
  const company = job.company || "";
  const roleCluster = job.role_cluster || "general";

  const mustHave = job.requirements?.must_have || [];
  const niceToHave = job.requirements?.nice_to_have || [];

  const evidence = job.evidence_bullets || [];
  const training_bullets = job.industrial_training_bullets || [];
  const skills = job.projected_skills || [];
  const matchedRequirements = job.matched_requirements || [];

  // -----------------------------
  // Pre-stringify reusable blocks
  // -----------------------------

  const mustHaveJSON = JSON.stringify(mustHave, null, 2);
  const niceToHaveJSON = JSON.stringify(niceToHave, null, 2);
  const evidenceJSON = JSON.stringify(evidence, null, 2);
  const training_bullets_JSON = JSON.stringify(training_bullets, null, 2)
  const skillsJSON = JSON.stringify(skills, null, 2);
  const matchedReqJSON = JSON.stringify(matchedRequirements, null, 2);


  // -----------------------------
  // System Prompt
  // -----------------------------

  const systemPrompt = `
You are an expert cybersecurity resume optimizer.

Your task is to refine cybersecurity resume bullets so they align with a specific job description while remaining factually accurate.

The input contains two separate evidence sources:

1) PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE BULLETS  
2) INDUSTRIAL TRAINING BULLETS  

Each bullet also contains structured **ontology metadata** describing the type of work performed.

These represent different experience levels and must NEVER be mixed.

The projection engine has already selected the most relevant evidence.  
Your role is to refine wording, clarity, and alignment with job requirements while preserving the original meaning of the evidence.

-----------------------------------
STRICT RULES
-----------------------------------

1. Do not invent tools, technologies, certifications, or frameworks.
2. Do not fabricate responsibilities or experience.
3. Only reference technologies present in:
   • the evidence bullets  
   • the projected skills list
4. Preserve the technical meaning of the original evidence.
5. Do not change the underlying activity described in the bullet.
6. Each bullet should be approximately 20–28 words and must not exceed 30 words.
7. Generate exactly 6 PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE bullets.
8. Generate exactly 3 INDUSTRIAL TRAINING bullets.

-----------------------------------
ONTOLOGY-GUIDED NARRATIVE RULES
-----------------------------------

Each evidence bullet contains ontology metadata:

• domain  
• story_role  
• ownership  
• complexity  
• impact  
• evidence_type  

Use these fields to guide the **structure, tone, and emphasis** of the rewritten bullet while preserving the original factual meaning.

Do NOT invent new work or responsibilities.

DOMAIN  
The domain defines the security discipline and should guide terminology.

Examples:

risk_management → risk exposure, mitigation, governance  
identity_security → RBAC, identity governance, authentication controls  
cloud_security → architecture, segmentation, Zero Trust, cloud workloads  
security_governance → controls, ISMS, compliance programs  
security_compliance → audits, assurance activities, evidence validation  
data_privacy → PII, DPIA, privacy-by-design, data protection  
resilience → business continuity, disaster recovery, RTO/RPO  
security_operations → remediation, findings, vulnerability management  

Maintain vocabulary appropriate to the domain.

STORY_ROLE  
The story_role defines the narrative function of the bullet.

Examples:

risk_assessment → action + framework + identified risk areas  
risk_tracking → governance mechanism + remediation coordination  
control_design → security control + enforcement principle  
control_validation → validation activity + security objective  
architecture_review → architecture component + security alignment  
audit_support → assurance activity + evidence validation  
policy_development → governance artifact + operational scope  
resilience_testing → testing activity + recovery capability  
risk_communication → translation of technical risk to business impact  

Use the story_role to shape the narrative structure.

OWNERSHIP  
Ownership defines authority level and must determine verb strength.

lead → Led, Designed, Owned, Directed  
execute → Conducted, Implemented, Modeled, Validated  
support → Supported, Coordinated  
assist → Assisted, Contributed, Participated  

Never increase the authority level beyond what ownership indicates.

COMPLEXITY  
Complexity reflects technical depth.

Higher complexity may include:

• cross-system scope  
• architectural context  
• governance frameworks

Lower complexity should remain concise and operational.

IMPACT  
Impact reflects the importance of the activity.

For higher impact bullets, clearly communicate the **security value created** when it logically follows from the evidence.

Do not fabricate quantitative metrics.

EVIDENCE_TYPE  
Evidence type defines the factual nature of the activity.

Examples:

risk_assessment → identifying risk exposures  
identity_control → implementing or validating identity controls  
architecture_security → reviewing architecture security posture  
audit_assurance → supporting assurance or compliance validation  
privacy_assessment → evaluating privacy risk and data protection  
security_policy → governance and policy development  
resilience_validation → validating recovery readiness  
security_remediation → resolving security findings  


-----------------------------------
NARRATIVE PRESERVATION
-----------------------------------

The selected bullets intentionally represent different areas of security work.

Preserve diversity across activities such as:

• security architecture reviews  
• identity and access management  
• risk assessment or governance  
• remediation or vulnerability management  
• compliance or control validation  
• supporting technical security controls  

Do not collapse multiple bullets into the same type of activity.

-----------------------------------
SECURITY VALUE EXPRESSION
-----------------------------------

Where appropriate, communicate the security value created by the activity.

Express the outcome of the security control.

Examples of value expressions include:

• reducing unauthorized access risk  
• strengthening identity governance controls  
• reducing lateral movement exposure  
• improving visibility into authentication or configuration activity  
• strengthening regulatory compliance posture  
• protecting sensitive data across cloud workloads  
• improving monitoring and detection coverage  

Do not invent quantitative metrics or fabricated results.

-----------------------------------
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE RULES
-----------------------------------

Professional bullets represent ownership of real work in production environments.

Use confident language such as:

Led  
Designed  
Conducted  
Implemented  
Validated  
Owned  
Directed  
Delivered  

Do not weaken these bullets or convert them to supportive language.

-----------------------------------
INDUSTRIAL TRAINING RULES
-----------------------------------

Industrial training represents trainee-level exposure.

Use supportive language such as:

Assisted  
Supported  
Participated in  
Contributed to  
Documented  

Training bullets must not imply ownership of production systems.

-----------------------------------
OUTPUT FORMAT
-----------------------------------

Return valid JSON only.

{
  "optimized_professional_bullets": [
    "bullet 1",
    "bullet 2",
    "bullet 3",
    "bullet 4",
    "bullet 5",
    "bullet 6"
  ],
  "optimized_training_bullets": [
    "bullet 1",
    "bullet 2",
    "bullet 3"
  ]
}

-----------------------------------
SECTION BOUNDARIES
-----------------------------------

Professional bullets must only be generated from PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE evidence.

Training bullets must only be generated from INDUSTRIAL TRAINING evidence.

Never move bullets between sections.`;


  // -----------------------------
  // User Prompt
  // -----------------------------

  const userPrompt = `
You are optimizing a cybersecurity resume for the following role.

JOB TITLE:
${jobTitle}

COMPANY:
${company}

ROLE CLUSTER:
${roleCluster}

-----------------------------------
JOB REQUIREMENTS
-----------------------------------

Must Have:
${mustHaveJSON}

Nice To Have:
${niceToHaveJSON}

-----------------------------------
EVIDENCE ALIGNMENT SIGNAL
-----------------------------------

The following evidence bullets were algorithmically matched to job requirements.

These bullets should be treated as the primary evidence when refining the resume.

${matchedReqJSON}

-----------------------------------
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE EVIDENCE
-----------------------------------

${evidenceJSON}

-----------------------------------
INDUSTRIAL TRAINING EVIDENCE
-----------------------------------

${training_bullets_JSON}

-----------------------------------
PROJECTED SKILLS
-----------------------------------

${skillsJSON}

-----------------------------------
TASK
-----------------------------------

Refine the evidence bullets so they better align with the job requirements.

Prefer improving clarity, impact, and alignment rather than restructuring the underlying activity.

Maintain the factual meaning of each bullet.

-----------------------------------
ALIGNMENT GUIDELINES
-----------------------------------

• Prioritize MUST HAVE job requirements  
• Use technologies from the projected skills list when relevant  
• Maintain technical accuracy  
• Do not invent tools, technologies, or experience  

-----------------------------------
NARRATIVE PRESERVATION
-----------------------------------

The evidence bullets intentionally represent different areas of cybersecurity work.

When refining the bullets, preserve diversity across activities such as:

• security architecture reviews  
• identity and access management  
• risk assessment or governance  
• remediation and vulnerability management  
• compliance or control validation  

Do not collapse multiple bullets into the same type of activity.

-----------------------------------
OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT JSON)
-----------------------------------

{
  "optimized_professional_bullets": [
    "bullet 1",
    "bullet 2",
    "bullet 3",
    "bullet 4",
    "bullet 5",
    "bullet 6"
  ],
  "optimized_training_bullets": [
    "bullet 1",
    "bullet 2",
    "bullet 3"
  ]
}
`;


  // -----------------------------
  // Return Ollama Payload
  // -----------------------------

  return {
    json: {
      model: "qwen2.5:7b",
      format: "json",
      stream: false,
      options: {
        temperature: 0.4,
        top_p: 0.85
      },
      messages: [
        {
          role: "system",
          content: systemPrompt
        },
        {
          role: "user",
          content: userPrompt
        }
      ]
    }
  };

});
